- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, model often underestimates the depth of decline — add 1–3% buffer below true low.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates volatility — smooth out extreme swings by reducing standard deviation by 15–20%.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overestimates momentum — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 7–10 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (e.g., -0.3 to 0.2), model tends to average out — use weighted average of recent 5-day sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
